# Toaster: `jl-toaster`

The corner of the window where toasts stack, and toast() to show one from anywhere.

- Class `JlToaster`, a organism: `import { JlToaster } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/toaster

The toaster is the place where toasts appear: a corner or an edge of the window, the newest nearest the
edge, at most max at a time (older ones wait for newer ones to close). It sits in the top layer, so its toasts show
over open dialogs too, and it is a polite live region: screen readers read each new toast without being cut off.

Most pages never write one: import toast from jlib and call toast({ heading, text, tone }) from anywhere. It
finds the page's toaster, or puts one at the end of the body the first time, and returns a handle whose dismiss()
closes the toast early. Its toasts close after 5 seconds (8 for an error, or with an action to press) and have a
close button, unless the options say otherwise. Write a jl-toaster in the page yourself to choose the placement: toast() then uses it.

## Use

```ts
import { JlToaster } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlToaster max={3} placement="bottom-right" />
```

```html
<jl-toaster max="3" placement="bottom-right"></jl-toaster>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `placement` (attribute `placement`): `'top-right' | 'top-center' | 'bottom-right' | 'bottom-center' | 'bottom-left'`, default `'bottom-right'`. Where the toasts stack.
- `max` (attribute `max`): `number`, default `3`. How many toasts show at once; the older ones wait.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The name of the region for screen readers. Empty: jlib's own text, in the language shown.

## Slots

- The default slot: The toasts; notify() and toast() add them here.

## Methods

- `notify(options: ToastOptions): ToastHandle`: Shows a toast in this toaster: 5 seconds and a close button unless the options say otherwise.
- `toast(options: ToastOptions): { update(changes: ToastOptions): void; dismiss(): void }`: A function, not a method: shows a toast in the page's toaster, made on first use. Options: heading, text, tone, icon, duration, closable, actionLabel, onAction, working, progress. The handle's update() changes them while it shows.
- `download(url: string, options?: DownloadOptions): Promise<DownloadResult>`: A function: downloads a file with its progress in a toast, and saves it under the name the server gives. Options: title, fileName, init (the request), texts (preparing, received, receivedOf, saved, failed, cancel, with {time}, {received}, {total}, {name}, {size} and {error}). Says how it ended.
- `downloadTexts(): DownloadTexts`: A function: the texts download() says unless its options give others, in jlib's language (jlTexts), their placeholders left to fill.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The region in the top layer that holds the toasts.
- `--width` (custom property): The width of the toasts: 380px.
- `--edge` (custom property): The distance from the edges of the window: 16px.
- `--edge-bottom` (custom property): The distance from the bottom for the bottom placements: --edge, above the tab bar of an app shell (--jl-shell-bottom).

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### Each tone

toast() from anywhere: the first call puts a toaster at the bottom right of the page.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-button class="tone-neutral" label="Neutral"></jl-button>
  <jl-button class="tone-ok" icon="circle-check" label="Saved"></jl-button>
  <jl-button class="tone-info" icon="info" label="Info"></jl-button>
  <jl-button class="tone-warn" icon="triangle-alert" label="Warning"></jl-button>
  <jl-button class="tone-danger" icon="circle-x" label="Error"></jl-button>
</div>
```

```js
import { toast } from '@syware/jlib';

root.querySelector('.tone-ok').events.register('press', () =>
  toast({ heading: 'Changes saved', text: 'Your profile is up to date.', tone: 'ok' })
);
root.querySelector('.tone-danger').events.register('press', () =>
  toast({ heading: 'Payment failed', text: 'The card was declined. Try another one.', tone: 'danger' })
);
// … one button per tone
```

### With an action

An action such as Undo: onAction runs, then the toast closes.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-button class="archive" icon="inbox" label="Archive the message"></jl-button>
</div>
```

```js
root.querySelector('.archive').events.register('press', () =>
  toast({
    heading: 'Message archived',
    text: 'It moved to the Archive folder.',
    actionLabel: 'Undo',
    duration: 8000,
    onAction: () => toast({ heading: 'Message restored', tone: 'ok' }),
  })
);
```

### Work in progress

A toast that stays (duration 0) while the work runs, its bar showing how far (working, progress), updated from code by its handle, then closing by itself once done.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-button class="upload" variant="primary" icon="upload" label="Upload report.pdf"></jl-button>
</div>
```

```js
const upload = toast({ heading: 'Uploading report.pdf', icon: 'upload', duration: 0, closable: false,
  working: true, progress: 0, text: '0 of 2.4 MB' });
// As the work goes on:
upload.update({ progress: 40, text: '1.0 of 2.4 MB' });
// Once it is done:
upload.update({ working: false, tone: 'ok', icon: '', text: 'Shared with the team.', duration: 5000,
  closable: true });
```

### Downloading a file

download() fetches a file with its progress in a toast: the time the server takes to prepare it, the bytes received, then the name it was saved under, or why it failed. Its Cancel stops it.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-button class="download" icon="download" label="Download the report"></jl-button>
</div>
```

```js
import { download } from '@syware/jlib';

root.querySelector('.download').events.register('press', () =>
  download('/api/reports/q3.csv', { title: 'Report of the quarter' })
);
```

### Placement

A toaster of your own decides where its toasts go: notify() shows one in it.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-button class="top" label="Notify at the top"></jl-button>
</div>
<jl-toaster class="top-toaster" placement="top-center" max="2"></jl-toaster>
```

```js
const toaster = root.querySelector('jl-toaster');
root.querySelector('.top').events.register('press', () =>
  toaster.notify({ heading: 'Connected', text: 'Live updates are on.', tone: 'info' })
);
```

### Over a dialog

In the top layer, toasts show over an open dialog.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-button class="open-settings" label="Open settings"></jl-button>
</div>
<jl-dialog class="settings" heading="Notifications" size="sm">
  <p>Save to see the toast over this dialog.</p>
  <jl-button slot="actions" class="save" variant="primary" label="Save"></jl-button>
</jl-dialog>
```

```js
const dialog = root.querySelector('jl-dialog');
root.querySelector('.open-settings').events.register('press', () => dialog.show());
root.querySelector('.save').events.register('press', () =>
  toast({ heading: 'Settings saved', tone: 'ok' })
);
```
